description: Canonical finding.violation_type values and their coaching guide basenames. Detector rules declare one flat reference into this vocabulary; the mapping itself stays beside the rule definition so project-local rules work and a mapping change stales that rule's receipt while guide prose does not.

notes: No dots: a guide file is resolved as <basename>.md or <basename>.<language>.md, so a dotted basename would be read as a language variant.
No subdirectories: both installer paths enumerate the guides directory non-recursively.
The leading underscore is reserved for the three presentation guides (_clean, _incomplete, _uncoached) and can never be claimed by a catalogued type.
Windows device names are reserved so the same flat asset set is installable on every supported filesystem.

historical:defect.summary: A defect recorded by a past learning or pitfall.

upstream:management-gap.summary: An upstream process or ownership gap outside this repository.

upstream:logic-bug.summary: A logic defect owned by an upstream component.

upstream:schema-drift.summary: An upstream schema or contract has drifted from its consumers.

repo:hygiene.summary: Repository hygiene: stale, duplicated, or misplaced material.

repo:regression.summary: Behaviour that previously worked and no longer does.

design:flaw.summary: A design decision that produces recurring defects.

measurement-gap.summary: A claim that cannot be checked because nothing measures it.

historical:guardrail.summary: An operational guardrail recorded by a past learning.

historical:root_cause.summary: A validated explanatory root cause promoted from history.

historical:tooling.summary: A Weave/runtime tooling defect promoted from history.

historical:finding.summary: Promoted from a source node already typed as a finding.

historical:learning-promotion.summary: Promoted from a learning with no more specific signal.

memory_contradiction.summary: Two memory or finding claims assert opposite polarity.

code:swallowed-exception.summary: A catch-all that discards the error hides a failure nobody has named.

code:unsafe-subprocess.summary: A subprocess invocation lets the shell reinterpret its arguments.

code:unquoted-expansion.summary: An unquoted expansion re-splits and globs its own value.

prose:generated-vocabulary.summary: High-frequency generated-text vocabulary decorates instead of informing.

prose:filler.summary: Filler and hedging phrases that carry no claim.

prose:unearned-significance.summary: Headings or scaffolding that announce importance the content does not carry.

prose:self-attested-virtue.summary: Text asserting its own rigour, completeness, or verification instead of showing it.

prose:work-context-leakage.summary: Session or process narration leaking into a durable document.

prose:punctuation-density.summary: A punctuation habit dense enough to read as a tic.

prose:register.summary: Register inappropriate to the document's audience.

markdown:malformed-markup.summary: Markup that renders differently than the author intended.

markdown:citation-integrity.summary: A citation that does not resolve to a real, dated reference.

markdown:metadata-formatting.summary: Metadata expressed as ad-hoc emphasis rather than structure.

absent_violation_type.detail: A finding node with no finding.violation_type stays readable and survives unrelated updates. The pre-close validator continues to require the field before close, and canonical quality promotion never emits an absent value.

emitters.policy: The scraped rule code is provenance, not a type. It must be recorded alongside a catalogued type rather than becoming the type itself; an unbounded type namespace has no guide and no review.
Writes finding metadata through a direct SQL INSERT, bypassing the update-path enum gate. The literal value is catalogued as-is rather than renamed so existing nodes stay valid without rewriting.
Enum-gated at write time against the projected vocabulary.
